html:
Aquincum was a Roman legionary fortress and town on the Danube in what is now the Óbuda district of Budapest, founded as a camp in the late first century and made capital of the province of Pannonia Inferior around 106.

It guarded the Danube frontier, the limes, against peoples beyond the river. A legion of about 6,000 men was based there, with a civilian town that had baths, two amphitheatres, temples and heated houses. A water organ found there, dated 228, is among the best preserved of its kind. The future emperor Hadrian served as governor. The town declined in the 300s as Huns and other peoples pressed in, and the Romans gave up Pannonia in the 400s. Its ruins are a museum park in Budapest.
sum: Aquincum was a Roman legionary fortress and town on the Danube in what is now the Óbuda district of Budapest, founded as a camp in the late first century and made capital of the province of Pannonia Inferior around 106.
